nodes.question: Who needs an account to use the app?

options.label: Nobody logs in — one person uses it on their own device
Exactly one person logs in (the owner)
Several people log in, possibly with different powers

nodes.question: Do different people have different powers?

options.label: Everyone who logs in can do everything
An owner/admin plus staff with fewer powers
Admins define their own roles and permissions

nodes.question: Do outside parties (customers, clients, vendors) use the app directly?

options.label: They open a secure link (no account needed)
They have their own accounts and log in

nodes.question: Is this for one business, or will many separate businesses use it with their data kept apart?

options.label: Many separate businesses, each seeing only its own data

nodes.question: How do additional people get access?
How do people sign in?
What happens when two people edit the same thing at once?

options.label: Common; the app must prevent or merge conflicting edits

nodes.question: Do you need a record of who changed what and when?

options.label: Just created/updated by whom and when
A full, viewable history of every change

nodes.question: How does the app reach people when something happens?

options.label: It doesn't — people check the app

nodes.question: Must it work without internet?

options.label: Keeps working offline and syncs later

nodes.question: Where is it used?

options.label: In a browser, on desktop and phone
In a browser, mostly on phones

nodes.question: Do you start with existing data?
Do people need to get their data out?
When something is deleted, what really happens?

options.label: It's archived and can be restored
Records are never deleted, only voided/cancelled

nodes.question: How much data will there be?
Does it need to connect to other tools?

options.label: A few key ones (e.g., accounting, payments, calendar)
Many — it needs a public API / webhooks

nodes.question: Languages and regions?
Can files/photos be attached to things?

options.label: Yes — with previews, versions, and sharing

nodes.question: Do some actions need someone else's approval first?
Must anything happen automatically on a schedule?

options.label: Records get created automatically (recurring invoices, appointments, reports)

nodes.question: Is any part visible to the public without logging in?

options.label: Yes — content people create is public

nodes.question: Does it hold data with special legal handling (health, payment cards, minors)?
How long is data kept?

options.label: Each business sets its own policy

nodes.question: Can each business customize the app?

options.label: No — everyone gets the same thing

nodes.question: What do people need to see across many records?

options.label: A dashboard with totals and counts

nodes.question: What can outside parties do when they access the app?

options.label: View what's theirs and act on it (pay, approve, book)
View everything that's theirs, including history
Full self-service: edit their details, create requests, message

nodes.question: Who sends invoices to whom?

options.label: The business bills its own clients
The business sends invoices on behalf of its clients to their customers

nodes.question: How are invoices numbered?

options.label: Strictly sequential per business (no gaps; legally safe)

nodes.question: Can an invoice change after it's sent?

options.label: No — corrections go through a credit note / new invoice

nodes.question: How do payments get recorded?

options.label: Someone marks invoices paid by hand
Clients pay online and it's recorded automatically

nodes.question: Can an invoice be paid in parts?

options.label: No — paid in full or not

nodes.question: How is tax handled on invoices?
One currency or several?
Recurring invoices (e.g., monthly retainers)?

options.label: Yes — created and sent automatically on a schedule

nodes.question: What happens when an invoice is overdue?

options.label: Someone sends a reminder by hand

nodes.question: Late fees?
Estimates/quotes before invoices?

options.label: Yes — and an accepted quote becomes an invoice

nodes.question: Corrections and refunds?

options.label: Credit notes plus refunds through the payment provider

nodes.question: How do invoices reach clients?

options.label: A link to an online invoice page (where they can also pay)
Email with PDF and a link

nodes.question: How detailed is the invoice lifecycle?

options.label: Draft → Sent → Viewed → Partially paid → Paid / Overdue / Void

nodes.question: Branding on invoices?
Deposits / retainers up front?

options.label: Yes — deposits that later apply to invoices

nodes.question: Are records grouped into separate projects/workspaces, or is it one shared pool?

options.label: One shared pool — everything lives in one place with filters
Separate projects/workspaces, each with its own members

nodes.question: Who can see a record?

options.label: Everyone in the team sees everything
Records are private to their owner unless shared or assigned
Visible within the owner's team/department; admins see all

nodes.question: Who can change a record?

options.label: Anyone who can see it can edit it
Only its owner/assignee and admins; others just view
Set per record: view / comment / edit

nodes.question: Are the fields on a record fixed, or can admins add their own?

options.label: Fixed — the same fields for everyone
Admins add custom fields (text, number, date, dropdown) to each record type
Admins define whole new record types with their own fields

nodes.question: Do records move through stages?

options.label: Yes — a fixed set of stages (e.g., Lead → Qualified → Won/Lost)
Yes — admins define stages and can have several pipelines

nodes.question: Are records assigned to people with deadlines?

options.label: One assignee and an optional due date
Several assignees plus watchers, with due dates and reminders

nodes.question: Can people discuss a record inside the app?

options.label: Comments with @mentions plus an automatic activity log of every change

nodes.question: Are records linked to each other?

options.label: Yes — records of different types reference each other (contact → company → deal)
Yes — including parent/child trees (projects → tasks → sub-tasks)

nodes.question: How do people look at their records?

options.label: List plus a board (cards in columns by stage)
All of the above, with saved personal and shared views

nodes.question: Should the app do things on its own when records change?

options.label: No — people do everything by hand
Simple rules: when X happens, notify/assign/change stage
Multi-step workflows with conditions and delays

nodes.question: Templates for new records/projects?

options.label: Yes — pre-filled templates (e.g., onboarding checklist, standard project)

nodes.question: Can two records be the same thing (same email, same serial number)?

options.label: The app warns about likely duplicates and offers to merge
A key field must be unique; duplicates are rejected

nodes.question: How do people find a record?

options.label: Filter and sort within each list
One search box across all record types
Search that also looks inside comments and attachments

nodes.question: Who gets told when a record changes?

options.label: Anyone who follows the record, with per-person preferences

nodes.question: Can people change many records at once?

options.label: No — one record at a time
Yes — select many and assign/move/tag/delete together

nodes.question: Do some records repeat on a schedule (weekly check-in, monthly inspection)?

options.label: Yes — they are created automatically on a schedule

nodes.question: What parts of firm settings are customizable per firm?

options.label: Also email templates and message wording

nodes.question: What formats can clients download invoices in?

options.label: PDF, CSV, and XML (for import in other systems)

nodes.question: Can clients view/edit their own profiles?
Are invoice numbers system-generated or user-editable?

options.label: Users can enter or edit numbers (validated for uniqueness)

cards.context: You want to keep track of where each invoice stands in your bookkeeping process.

options.label: No — just a status flag (open/closed)
options.scenario: You see each invoice as either open or closed, with a simple status showing if it's active or finished. Bookkeepers work without extra steps or labels.

options.label: Yes — a fixed set of stages (e.g., Lead → Qualified → Won/Lost)
options.scenario: You and your bookkeepers move invoices through a clear set of steps, such as Draft, Sent, and Paid, making it easy to see progress at a glance.

also_sets: Edits are rare and whoever finishes last keeps their changes
You can handle hundreds of invoices without trouble
App stays in one language and country
You don't require formal approvals for invoices
Only ordinary business details are stored

cards.context: Your bookkeeping firm is preparing invoices for clients and considering how your team communicates about each record.

options.label: Comments on each record
options.scenario: You and your bookkeepers leave notes and discuss details directly on each invoice or client profile, keeping the conversation organized and visible for future reference.

options.label: No — just the fields
options.scenario: You and your team rely on invoice details and client information alone, discussing any questions or issues outside the app through calls, emails, or meetings.

also_sets: You email people when you need to reach them.
You can upload and download files for each record.
Each invoice has one tax rate.
You issue credit notes to correct or refund invoices.
Invoices are sent as PDFs attached to emails.

cards.context: Some clients occasionally pay invoices after the due date.

options.label: Added by hand when needed
options.scenario: You or your team add late fees to overdue invoices whenever you decide it's appropriate, and clients see these fees on their bills.

options.label: No
options.scenario: No late fees are ever added to overdue invoices, and clients never see extra charges for paying late.

also_sets: Bookkeepers and clients sign in with email and password
You track who created and changed invoices
You reach clients by email
You and clients can download invoice lists
Invoices are archived and can be restored

cards.context: Clients want to download their invoices after receiving them from your bookkeeping firm.

options.label: PDF only
options.scenario: Your client saves a copy of their invoice as a PDF to share or print, seeing it just as it appears on the screen.

options.label: PDF and CSV
options.scenario: Your client chooses to download their invoice as a PDF for easy viewing or as a CSV file to open and analyze in a spreadsheet.

also_sets: When a client wants a copy for their records: They get it in PDF only or PDF and CSV format.
When a client needs to import invoice data elsewhere: They can use a CSV file or not.
When clients ask for a spreadsheet: You can provide it or not.

cards.context: You want to decide what happens when someone deletes an invoice or profile in your invoicing app.

options.label: It's archived and can be restored
options.scenario: You archive the invoice or profile, so you or your team can find and restore it later if needed. Clients do not see archived items.

options.label: It's gone
options.scenario: When you delete an invoice or profile, it disappears completely, and neither you nor your team can get it back.

also_sets: You control who can view or restore deleted records
Deleted items no longer show to clients or bookkeepers
Admins can oversee deleted records if needed

cards.context: Bookkeeping firms are starting to use your invoicing app to manage their client billing.

options.label: No — people do everything by hand
options.scenario: Bookkeepers and administrators personally handle every step, from updating invoice statuses to notifying clients, ensuring full control over each task.

options.label: Simple rules: when X happens, notify/assign/change stage
options.scenario: When a bookkeeper marks an invoice as sent, clients automatically get an email; reassigning a client instantly notifies the new bookkeeper, reducing manual follow-up.

also_sets: Bookkeepers and administrators track actions themselves or rely on automatic notifications.
App shows who made changes and when, but not why.
Data can be exported as CSV or Excel spreadsheets.
No integrations with other software.

cards.context: Bookkeepers sometimes forget to follow up on unpaid invoices.

options.label: Only reminders/notifications
options.scenario: You and your clients receive periodic reminders about overdue invoices, prompting action without manual follow-up.

options.label: No
options.scenario: You rely on your team to track and follow up on unpaid invoices, with no automatic reminders sent to anyone.

also_sets: Everyone signs in with email and password
You see who created or updated records and when
You can download lists as CSV or Excel
The app handles hundreds of records smoothly
No connection to other tools

cards.context: Bookkeepers sometimes need to update invoices after sending them to clients.

options.label: Just created/updated by whom and when
options.scenario: You see who created or last updated an invoice and when, letting you track basic changes without details.

options.label: A full, viewable history of every change
options.scenario: You can review a timeline showing every change made to an invoice, including what was changed, who did it, and when.

also_sets: You sign in with email and password
You can download lists as CSV or Excel
No other tools connect
You can change sent invoices until paid
Each invoice uses a single tax rate

cards.context: Your bookkeeping firm is deciding how team members access invoice records.

options.label: Everyone in the team sees everything
options.scenario: Every bookkeeper in your firm can see all invoices and client profiles—anyone can check or update any record, regardless of who created it.

options.label: Records are private to their owner unless shared or assigned
options.scenario: Each bookkeeper only sees invoices and client profiles for their assigned clients; records stay private unless you specifically share them with another team member.

also_sets: Clients never see pages meant for your firm
Everyone signs in with email and password
You can see who created or updated each record and when
You start with a spreadsheet import
You can export lists as CSV or Excel

identity_provider.context: Your bookkeeping firm needs a way for employees and clients to access the invoicing app securely.

options.label: Email + password
options.scenario: You and your clients set up accounts with your email addresses and create unique passwords to sign in each time.

options.label: Google/Microsoft sign-in
options.scenario: You and your clients sign in quickly using your existing Google or Microsoft accounts, without needing to create new passwords.

also_sets: You download invoice lists as CSV or Excel files.
PDF invoices are sent as email attachments.
Only assigned users and admins can take actions; others just view.
Lists are sortable and filterable to help you find information.
